headline: 4 val images are byte-identical to train images, so the validation metric is untrustworthy — re-split before training, or you will retrain after the fact.
training_impact: Training will run fine (no NaNs, no structural or geometry defects), but the val set contains 4 images the model has seen in training, so every val metric is inflated by an unknown margin and cannot be used to compare checkpoints or decide readiness. Additionally, 3 duplicated boxes in train double-count in the loss, and 2 near-duplicate train pairs slightly over-weight their scenes.

decisions.rationale: Exact detector, sha1-verified: val/214827540762, val/382780712741, val/438274936455, val/889941193761 are byte-identical to train/000000476787, train/000000056127, train/000000080932, train/000000166166 respectively. The model trains on these exact images and is then scored on them, so the val number is optimistic by an unknown margin and meaningless for go/no-go decisions. Fix: remove the 4 val images (or re-split by content hash) before any training run — fixing this later means retraining.

Exact detector: 3 label files each list the same box twice (e.g. train/000000231822 line 6 repeats line 4). Duplicated boxes double-count in the loss and break the one-target-per-object assumption of NMS-free matchers, biasing training on those objects. Fix: delete the repeated lines in train/000000231822, train/000000255917, train/000000462756. Small in scale (3 boxes of 6815) but a real defect, and trivial to fix alongside the re-split.

Exact detector: 2 near-identical pairs inside train (one at perceptual distance 0/64, i.e. effectively identical; one at 1/64). Duplicates inside train over-weight whatever those scenes contain and inflate the reported dataset size. All 4 files are in train, so the val metric is not affected by this. Fix: drop one image from each pair (train/000000150638 vs train/912024475486; train/000000295420 vs train/303522373741) during the same cleanup pass.
